A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lipid bodies are produced in the cytosol of the labellar cells, and are then transported to the plasmalemmal surface, and finally accumulate between the plasmalemmas of adjacent cells, and between the plasmalemma and cuticle.
the lipid globules are formed by the labellum cells, and then the globules coalesce to form the labellar secretion.
Maxillaria acuiminata, M. cerifra, M. notyloglossa and M. cf. Notyloglossa produce a viscid labellar secretion that is rich in lipid and protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the labella of these species produce a wax-like secretion that consists of lipid and protein and is produced by a process involving the transfer of lipid through the cell wall.
the labellar lipids are not produced within specialized secretory cells but rather are produced by all epidermal cells.
the labellum is a highly modified organ in the genus Maxillaria and the secretions are produced by a complex process that is still not fully understood.
